title: Stopping Is Not the Limit: Understanding and Eliciting Agent Capability in Long-Horizon Vulnerability Exploitation
abstract: arXiv:2611.22888v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Vulnerability exploitation tests whether language model agents can develop working exploits from known software flaws. Sequential test-time scaling can improve exploitation performance, but larger budgets do not ensure sustained exploration: agents often stop with budget remaining. Yet what happens when execution continues beyond stopping remains underexplored. We investigate this gap on ExploitBench using DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 and MiMo-V2.6-Pro. We find additional verified gains after the first stop response, but gains diminish over longer execution. We identify two patterns associated with less productive continuation: an increasing proportion of stop responses within the same context and earlier stopping associated with summaries retaining impossibility judgments about unachieved capabilities. translated_title: 停止并非极限：理解并激发智能体在长程漏洞利用中的能力
translated_abstract: 漏洞利用测试的是语言模型智能体能否基于已知软件缺陷开发出可用的攻击利用代码。顺序式测试时扩展可以提升漏洞利用性能，但更大的预算并不保证持续的探索：智能体常常在预算尚有剩余时就停止。然而，当执行在停止之后继续进行时会发生什么，这一问题仍未得到充分研究。我们在 ExploitBench 上使用 DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 和 MiMo-V2.6-Pro 对这一空白展开了研究。我们发现，在首次停止响应之后仍可获得额外的经验证的收益，但收益随执行时间的延长而递减。我们识别出与低效续跑相关的两种模式：同一上下文中停止响应比例的不断增加，以及更早停止与摘要中保留的关于未实现能力的不可能性判断相关。为检验上下文管理能否激发更多能力，我们提出了 SCoRe，它在停止爆发点压缩上下文并标记这些 ju…（原文摘要在此处截断）
tldr: 该论文发现漏洞利用智能体在首次停止后继续执行仍能带来额外收益，并提出上下文压缩方法 SCoRe 以激发智能体在长程漏洞利用任务中的潜在能力。
en_tdlr: This paper shows that vulnerability exploitation agents can still achieve verified gains beyond their first stop response, and proposes SCoRe, a context-compaction approach, to elicit further latent agent capability in long-horizon exploitation tasks.
